value.zh: 拜太子左庶子，領書侍御史如故。
value.en: He was appointed Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent while still serving as Attendant Censor of the Masters of Writing.
value.literal: He was appointed Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent while still serving as Attendant Censor of the Masters of Writing.

value.zh: 皇太子虛襟敬憚。
value.en: The Crown Prince treated him with open respect and restraint.
value.literal: The Crown Prince opened his breast to him in respect and fear.

value.zh: 時唐令則為左庶子，太子昵狎之，每令以弦歌教內人。
value.en: At that time Tang Lingze was Left Assistant; the Crown Prince was intimate with him and often had him teach the inner household with string music.
value.literal: At that time Tang Lingze was Left Assistant; the Crown Prince was intimate with him and often had him teach the inner household with string music.

value.zh: 行本責之曰：「庶子當匡太子以正道，何嬖昵房帷之間哉！」
value.en: Xingben reproached him, saying, "The Assistant should guide the Crown Prince by the upright Way—why dally in fond intimacy within the bedchamber"!
value.literal: Xingben reproached him, saying: "The Assistant should guide the Crown Prince by the upright Way—why dally in fond intimacy within the bedchamber"!

value.zh: 令則甚慚而不能改。
value.en: Lingze was deeply ashamed but could not change.
value.literal: Lingze was greatly ashamed but could not change.

value.zh: 時沛國劉臻、平原明克讓、河南陸爽等並以文學為太子所親。
value.en: At that time Liu Zhen of Pei, Ming Keyang of Pingyuan, Lu Shuang of Henan, and others were all favored by the Crown Prince for their literary learning.
value.literal: At that time Liu Zhen of Pei, Ming Keyang of Pingyuan, Lu Shuang of Henan, and others were all favored by the Crown Prince for their literary learning.

value.zh: 行本怒其不能調護，每謂三人曰：「卿等正解讀書耳。」
value.en: Xingben was angry that they could not guide and protect the prince, and often said to the three, "You gentlemen only know how to read books, that is all".
value.literal: Xingben was angry that they could not guide and protect him, and often said to the three: "You gentlemen only know how to read books, that is all".

value.zh: 時左術率長史夏侯福為太子所昵，嘗於閤內與太子戲。
value.en: At that time Chief Clerk of the Left Guard Xiahou Fu was favored by the Crown Prince and once played with the Crown Prince inside the pavilion.
value.literal: At that time Chief Clerk of the Left Guard Xiahou Fu was favored by the Crown Prince and once played with the Crown Prince inside the pavilion.

value.zh: 福大笑，聲聞於外。
value.en: Fu laughed loudly, and the sound was heard outside.
value.literal: Fu laughed loudly, and the sound was heard outside.

value.zh: 行本時在閤下聞之，待其出，數之曰：「汝何小人，敢為褻慢！」
value.en: Xingben was below the pavilion and heard it; when Fu came out he rebuked him, saying, "What sort of petty man dares behave with such disrespect"!
value.literal: Xingben was below the pavilion and heard it; when Fu came out he counted his faults, saying: "What sort of petty man dares behave with such disrespect"!

value.zh: 因付執法者推之。
value.en: He then handed him over to the law officers for investigation.
value.literal: He then handed him over to the law officers for investigation.

value.zh: 太子為請，乃釋之。
value.en: The Crown Prince pleaded for him, and only then was he released.
value.literal: The Crown Prince pleaded for him, and only then was he released.

value.zh: 太子嘗得良馬，令福乘而觀之。
value.en: The Crown Prince once obtained a fine horse and had Fu ride it to show it off.
value.literal: The Crown Prince once obtained a fine horse and had Fu ride it to show it off.

value.zh: 太子甚悅，因欲令行本復乘。
value.en: The Crown Prince was greatly pleased and therefore wished to have Xingben ride it as well.
value.literal: The Crown Prince was greatly pleased and therefore wished to have Xingben ride it again.

value.zh: 行本正色曰：「至尊置臣於庶子位，欲輔導殿下以正道，非為殿下作弄臣。」
value.en: Xingben said sternly, "Your Majesty placed me in the post of Assistant to the Heir Apparent to guide the Crown Prince by the upright Way, not to be a plaything for the Crown Prince".
value.literal: Xingben said sternly: "Your Majesty placed me in the post of Assistant to the Heir Apparent to guide the Crown Prince by the upright Way, not to be a plaything for the Crown Prince".

value.zh: 太子慚而止。
value.en: The Crown Prince was ashamed and stopped.
value.literal: The Crown Prince was ashamed and stopped.

value.zh: 復以本官領大興令，權貴憚其方正，無敢至其門者。
value.en: He again held his original office and concurrently served as Magistrate of Daxing; the powerful and noble feared his uprightness, and none dared come to his gate.
value.literal: He again held his original office and concurrently served as Magistrate of Daxing; the powerful and noble feared his uprightness, and none dared come to his gate.

value.zh: 由是請托路絕，吏人懷之。
value.en: Because of this the path of private requests was cut off, and clerks and commoners cherished him.
value.literal: Because of this the path of private requests was cut off, and clerks and people cherished him.

value.zh: 未幾，卒於官，上甚傷惜之。
value.en: Before long he died in office, and the Emperor deeply mourned his loss.
value.literal: Before long he died in office, and the Emperor deeply mourned and regretted it.

value.zh: 及太子廢，上曰：「嗟乎！
value.en: When the Crown Prince was deposed, the Emperor said, "Alas!
value.literal: When the Crown Prince was deposed, the Emperor said: "Alas!

value.zh: 若使劉行本在，勇當不及此乎！」
value.en: If Liu Xingben were still alive, would Prince Yong not have come to this"!
value.literal: If Liu Xingben were still alive, would Prince Yong not have come to this"!

value.zh: 行本無子。
value.en: Xingben had no son.
value.literal: Xingben had no son.

value.zh: 齊武王
value.en: Prince Martial of Qi (Liu Yan)
value.literal: Prince Martial of Qi

value.zh: 初，臨邑侯復好學，能文章。
value.en: Liu Fu, marquis of Linyi, was a devoted scholar and a polished writer.
value.literal: In the beginning the marquis of Linyi, Fu, loved learning and was capable at composition.

value.zh: 永平中，每有講學事，輒令復典掌焉。
value.en: During Yongping he was routinely put in charge of court lectures and academies.
value.literal: In the Yongping period, whenever there were affairs of lecturing and learning, he was always ordered to take charge of them.

value.zh: 與班固、賈逵共述漢史，傅毅等皆宗事之。
value.en: With Ban Gu and Jia Kui he compiled Han history, while Fu Yi and others looked to him as their patron.
value.literal: Together with Ban Gu and Jia Kui he narrated Han history, and Fu Yi and others all took him as their teacher in service.

value.zh: 復子騊駼及從兄平望侯毅，並有才學。
value.en: His son Taotu and his cousin Yi, marquis of Pingwang, were likewise gifted scholars.
value.literal: Fu’s son Taotu and his elder male cousin Yi, marquis of Pingwang, both had talent and learning.

value.zh: 永寧中，鄧太后召毅及騊駼入東觀，與謁者僕射劉珍著中興以下名臣列士傳。
value.en: Under Yongning the Deng regent brought Yi and Taotu into the Eastern Library to join Liu Zhen in drafting biographies of notable men since the restoration.
value.literal: In the Yongning period Empress Dowager Deng summoned Yi and Taotu into the Eastern View, where with the herald superintendent Liu Zhen they wrote biographies of famous ministers and stalwarts from the restoration onward.

value.zh: 騊駼又自造賦、頌、書、論凡四篇。
value.en: Taotu also wrote four original pieces—fu, hymns, letters, and essays.
value.literal: Taotu moreover himself composed in all four pieces of rhapsody, eulogy, letter, and discourse.

value.zh: 平後坐與諸王交通，國除。
value.en: Ping later lost his title for illicit dealings with other princes.
value.literal: Later Ping sat guilty of trafficking with the various kings and the kingdom was abolished.

value.zh: 永平五年，顯宗更封平為竟陵侯。
value.en: In Yongping 5 Emperor Ming transferred Ping to the marquisate of Jingling.
value.literal: In the fifth year of Yongping the Manifest Ancestor changed the enfeoffment of Ping to be marquis of Jingling.

value.zh: 平卒，子真嗣。
value.en: Ping was succeeded by his son Zhen.
value.literal: When Ping died, his son Zhen succeeded.

value.zh: 真卒，子禹嗣。
value.en: Zhen was followed by Yu.
value.literal: When Zhen died, his son Yu succeeded.

value.zh: 禹卒，子嘉嗣。
value.en: Yu was followed by Jia.
value.literal: When Yu died, his son Jia succeeded.

value.zh: 列傳第六十 忠義二 ○吳僧哥 烏古論德升 張順 馬驤 伯德窊哥 奧屯醜和尚 從坦 孛朮魯福壽 吳邦傑 納合蒲剌都 女奚烈斡出 時茂先 溫蒂罕老兒 梁持勝 賈邦獻 移剌阿里合 完顏六斤 紇石烈鶴壽 蒲察婁室 女奚烈資祿 趙益 侯小叔 王佐 黃摑九住 烏林答乞住 陀滿斜烈 尼厖古蒲魯虎 兀顏畏可 兀顏訛出虎 粘割貞
value.en: Biographies 60: Loyalty and Righteousness II — Wu Sengge, Wugulun Desheng, Zhang Shun, Ma Xiang, Bode Wage, Aotun Chouheshang, Cong Tan, Beipailu Fushou, Wu Bangjie, Nahe Puladu, Nuxilie Wochu, Shi Maoxian, Wendihan Lao'er, Liang Chisheng, Jia Bangxian, Yila Alihe, Wanyan Liujin, Geshilie Heshou, Pucha Loushi, Nuxilie Zilu, Zhao Yi, Hou Xiaoshu, Wang Zuo, Huangguai Jiuzhu, Wulinda Qizhu, Tuoman Xielie, Nilanggupuluhu, Wuyan Weike, Wuyan Echuhu, and Zhange Zhen
value.literal: Biographies 60: Loyalty and Righteousness II ○ Wu Sengge, Wugulun Desheng, Zhang Shun, Ma Xiang, Bode Wage, Aotun Chouheshang, Cong Tan, Beipailu Fushou, Wu Bangjie, Nahe Puladu, Nuxilie Wochu, Shi Maoxian, Wendihan Lao'er, Liang Chisheng, Jia Bangxian, Yila Alihe, Wanyan Liujin, Geshilie Heshou, Pucha Loushi, Nuxilie Zilu, Zhao Yi, Hou Xiaoshu, Wang Zuo, Huangguai Jiuzhu, Wulinda Qizhu, Tuoman Xielie, Nilanggupuluhu, Wuyan Weike, Wuyan Echuhu, Zhange Zhen

value.zh: 賈邦獻，霍州霍邑縣陳村人也。
value.en: Jia Bangxian was from Chen Village in Huoyi County, Huozhou.
value.literal: Jia Bangxian was a native of Chen Village in Huoyi County, Huozhou.

value.zh: 舉進士第。
value.en: He passed the jinshi examination.
value.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.

value.zh: 質直有勇略。
value.en: He was upright by nature and possessed courage and strategic sense.
value.literal: He was upright by nature and possessed courage and strategy.

value.zh: 大元攻河東，邦獻集居民為守禦計。
value.en: When Yuan forces attacked Hedong, Bangxian gathered the residents to organize a defense.
value.literal: When Great Yuan forces attacked Hedong, Bangxian gathered the residents to plan defense.

value.zh: 既而，兵大至，居民悉降。
value.en: Before long a large army arrived and the residents all surrendered.
value.literal: Before long the army arrived in force and the residents all surrendered.

value.zh: 邦獻棄其家，獨與子懿保于松平寨。
value.en: Bangxian abandoned his household and alone with his son Yi took refuge at Songping Stockade.
value.literal: Bangxian abandoned his household and alone with his son Yi took refuge at Songping Stockade.

value.zh: 是時，權知州事劉珍在寨，與之共守，竟能成功。
value.en: At that time Liu Zhen, acting prefect, was at the stockade; together they held it and succeeded in the end.
value.literal: At this time Liu Zhen, acting prefect, was at the stockade; together they defended it and in the end succeeded.

value.zh: 珍每欲辟之，邦獻輒以衰老為辭。
value.en: Whenever Zhen wished to recruit him, Bangxian declined on grounds of old age.
value.literal: Whenever Zhen wished to recruit him, Bangxian declined on the grounds of old age.

value.zh: 興定四年十月，兵複大至，病不能避，與懿俱被執。
value.en: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Xingding the army came again in force. Too ill to escape, he and Yi were both captured.
value.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Xingding the army came again in force; ill and unable to escape, he and Yi were both captured.

value.zh: 欲以為鎮西元帥，且持刃脅之，邦獻不屈，密遣懿歸松平，遂自剄。
value.en: They wished to make him Marshal of the West and threatened him with blades. Bangxian refused, secretly sent Yi back to Songping, and cut his own throat.
value.literal: They wished to make him Marshal of the West and moreover threatened him with blades; Bangxian would not submit, secretly sent Yi back to Songping, and then cut his own throat.

value.zh: 贈奉直大夫、本縣令。
value.en: He was posthumously made Grand Master of Direct Service and magistrate of his home county.
value.literal: He was posthumously awarded Grand Master of Direct Service and Magistrate of his home county.

value.zh: 孝惠皇帝諱衷，字正度，武帝第二子也。
value.en: Emperor Hui, whose personal name was Sima Zhong and courtesy name Zhengdu, was Emperor Wu’s second son.
value.literal: The Filial and Kind Emperor, taboo name Zhong, courtesy name Zhengdu, was the second son of Emperor Wu.

value.zh: 泰始三年，立爲皇太子，時年九歲。
value.en: In 267, when he was nine years old, he was named heir apparent.
value.literal: In the third year of Taishi, he was established as crown prince; at the time he was nine sui.

value.zh: 太熙元年四月己酉，武帝崩。
value.en: In the fourth month of the first year of Taixi, on the day jiyou, Emperor Wu died.
value.literal: In the first year of Taixi, on the jiyou day of the fourth month, Emperor Wu died.

value.zh: 是日，皇太子即皇帝位，大赦，改元爲永熙。
value.en: That same day the heir apparent ascended the throne, ordered a general amnesty, and adopted the reign title Yongxi.
value.literal: That same day the crown prince assumed the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yongxi.

value.zh: 尊皇后楊氏曰皇太后，立妃賈氏爲皇后。
value.en: Empress Yang was elevated to empress dowager, and his consort Lady Jia was installed as empress.
value.literal: The empress, Lady Yang, was honored as empress dowager; Consort Jia was established as empress.

value.zh: 六月戊辰，大赦，增吏位二等。
value.en: The wuchen day in the sixth month brought a general amnesty and a two-grade promotion for every official.
value.literal: In the sixth month, on the wuchen day, a general amnesty; officials’ ranks were increased two grades.

value.zh: 復封賓徒王晏爲吳王。
value.en: Prince Yan of Bintu was restored to the old Wu princedom.
value.literal: Prince Yan of Bintu was again enfeoffed as prince of Wu.

value.zh: 庚午，東萊王蕤、左衛將軍王輿謀廢齊王冏，事泄，蕤廢爲庶人，輿伏誅，夷三族。
value.en: Prince Rui of Donglai and Wang Yu conspired to topple Prince Jiong; when the plot surfaced, Rui was reduced to commoner rank while Wang Yu and three degrees of his kin were executed.
value.literal: On the gengwu day, Prince Rui of Donglai and General of the Left Guards Wang Yu plotted to depose Prince Jiong of Qi; the affair leaked; Rui was deposed to commoner status; Yu submitted to execution; three clans were exterminated.

value.zh: 甲戌，以齊王冏爲大司馬、都督中外諸軍事，成都王穎爲大將軍、錄尚書事，河間王顒爲太尉。
value.en: Prince Jiong became grand marshal and commander-in-chief, Prince Ying general-in-chief with charge of the secretariat, and Prince Yong grand commandant on the jiaxu day.
value.literal: On the jiaxu day, Prince Jiong of Qi was made grand marshal and area commander for all military affairs within and without; Prince Ying of Chengdu was made general-in-chief and recorder of secretariat affairs; Prince Yong of Hejian was made grand commandant.

value.zh: 罷丞相，復置司徒官。
value.en: The chancellorship was abolished and the ministry of education revived.
value.literal: The chancellor was abolished; the office of minister of education was re-established.

value.zh: 己卯，以梁王肜爲太宰，領司徒。
value.en: Prince Rong of Liang was named grand steward while retaining the ministry of education on the jimao day.
value.literal: On the jimao day, Prince Xiong of Liang was made grand steward, concurrently heading the ministry of education.

value.zh: 封齊王冏功臣葛旟牟平公，路季小黃公，衛毅平陰公，劉真安鄉公，韓泰封丘公。
value.en: Prince Jiong of Qi's meritorious followers were enfeoffed: Ge Yu as Duke of Mouping, Lu Ji as Duke of Xiaohuang, Wei Yi as Duke of Pingyin, Liu Zhen as Duke of Anxiang, and Han Tai as Duke of Fengqiu.
value.literal: Prince Jiong of Qi’s meritorious subjects Ge Yu was enfeoffed duke of Mouping, Lu Ji duke of Xiaohuang, Wei Yi duke of Pingyin, Liu Zhen duke of Anxiang, and Han Tai duke of Fengqiu.

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 九年六月，有桑生於宮西廂，日長尺餘，數日而枯。
value.en: In the sixth lunar month of the ninth year, a mulberry sprouted in the palace’s west wing. It grew more than a chi each day, then withered after several days.
value.literal: In the sixth lunar month of the ninth year, a mulberry sprouted in the west wing of the palace; it grew more than a chi each day and withered after several days.

value.zh: 十二月，賈后將廢太子，詐稱上不和，呼太子入朝。
value.en: Twelfth month Jia feigned imperial illness to lure Yu to court.
value.literal: In the twelfth month, when Empress Jia would depose the crown prince, she falsely claimed the emperor was unwell and summoned the crown prince to court.

value.zh: 既至，後不見，置於別室，遣婢陳舞賜以酒棗，逼飲醉之。
value.en: She hid him, fed him wine and dates through Chen Wu until he was drunk.
value.literal: When he arrived she did not receive him but lodged him in a side chamber, sent maid Chen Wu with ale and jujubes, and forced him drunk.

value.zh: 使黃門侍郎潘岳作書草，若禱神之文，有如太子素意，因醉而書之，令小婢承福以紙筆及書草使太子書之。
value.en: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the Crown Prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.
value.literal: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the crown prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.

value.zh: 文曰：「陛下宜自了；
value.en: The text read: "Your Majesty should end your own life;
value.literal: The text read: "Your Majesty should end your own life;

value.zh: 不自了，吾當入了之。
value.en: Or I will finish you.
value.literal: if you do not end it yourself, I shall come in and end it for you.

value.zh: 中宮又宜速自了；
value.en: The empress too should quickly end her own life;
value.literal: The empress too should quickly end her own life;

value.zh: 不了，吾當手了之。
value.en: Or I will kill her myself.
value.literal: if she does not, I shall end her life with my own hands.

value.zh: 並謝妃共要克期而兩發，勿疑猶豫，致後患。
value.en: Consort Xie and I strike together—no delay.
value.literal: Together with Consort Xie we agreed a joint date for simultaneous rising—do not hesitate and breed later trouble.

value.zh: 茹毛飲血於三辰之下，皇天許當掃除患害，立道文為王，蔣為內主。
value.en: We shall eat raw flesh and drink blood beneath the three luminaries; High Heaven grants us leave to sweep away the scourge, enthrone Daowen as king, and install Jiang as inner mistress.
value.literal: We shall eat raw flesh and drink blood beneath the three luminaries; High Heaven grants us leave to sweep away the scourge, enthrone Daowen as king, and install Jiang as inner mistress.

value.zh: 願成，當三牲祠北君，大赦天下。
value.en: Then sacrifice to the Northern Lord and amnesty all.
value.literal: When wish is fulfilled we shall sacrifice three victims to the Northern Lord and proclaim an empire-wide amnesty.

value.zh: 要疏如律令。」
value.en: So commands the spell.'
value.literal: Let this sworn petition take effect as commanded.

value.zh: 太子醉迷不覺，遂依而寫之，其字半不成。
value.en: Too drunk and confused to realize what he was doing, the crown prince copied it, but half the characters were incomplete.
value.literal: The crown prince was too drunk and confused to notice; he copied accordingly; half the characters failed to form.

value.zh: 既而補成之，后以呈帝。
value.en: Helpers patched characters before Jia showed Hui.
value.literal: They afterward filled them in; the empress presented it to the emperor.

value.zh: 帝幸式乾殿，召公卿入，使黃門令董猛乙太子書及青紙詔曰：「遹書如此，今賜死。」
value.en: The emperor visited Shi-Qian Hall, summoned dukes and ministers, and had Yellow Gate Chief Dong Meng display the crown prince's script with an edict on blue paper: "Yu has written thus—now sentence him to death."
value.literal: The emperor visited Shi-Qian Hall, summoned dukes and ministers, and had Yellow Gate Chief Dong Meng display the crown prince's script with an edict on blue paper: 'Yu has written thus—now sentence him to death.'

value.zh: 遍示諸公王，莫有言者，惟張華、裴頠證明太子。
value.en: Silence fell until Zhang Hua and Pei Wei defended Yu.
value.literal: No one among lords and dukes spoke except Zhang Hua and Pei Wei who verified the crown prince's innocence.

value.zh: 賈后使董猛矯以長廣公主辭白帝曰：「事宜速決，而群臣各有不同，若有不從詔，宜以軍法從事。」
value.en: Empress Jia had Dong Meng falsely relay Princess Changguang's words to the emperor: "Matters must be settled quickly while ministers disagree—whoever disobeys the edict should face military law."
value.literal: Empress Jia had Dong Meng falsely relay Princess Changguang's words to the emperor: 'Matters must be settled quickly while ministers disagree—whoever disobeys the edict should face military law.'

value.zh: 議至日西不決。
value.en: Debate stalled till dusk.
value.literal: Deliberation lasted until sunset unresolved.

value.zh: 後懼事變，乃表免太子為庶人，詔許之。
value.en: Jia feared delay—demoted Yu to commoner instead.
value.literal: The empress feared events might shift and therefore memorialized to degrade the crown prince to commoner status; an edict approved.

value.zh: 於是使尚書和郁持節，解結為副，及大將軍梁王肜、鎮東將軍淮南王允、前將軍東武公澹、趙王倫、太保何劭詣東宮，廢太子為庶人。
value.en: Thereupon Minister He Yu was dispatched with insignia, with Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Sima Rong, Prince of Liang; Eastern Garrison General Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan; Forward General Sima Dan, Duke of Dongwu; Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao; and Grand Guardian He Shao. They went to the Eastern Palace to depose the crown prince as a commoner.
value.literal: Thereupon Minister He Yu was dispatched with insignia, with Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Sima Rong, Prince of Liang; Eastern Garrison General Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan; Forward General Sima Dan, Duke of Dongwu; Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao; and Grand Guardian He Shao. They went to the Eastern Palace to depose the crown prince as a commoner.

value.zh: 是日太子游玄圃，聞有使者至，改服出崇賢門，再拜受詔，步出承華門，乘粗犢車。
value.en: That day the crown prince roamed the Mystic Garden; hearing envoys arrived he changed clothes, exited Chongxian Gate, twice bowed receiving the edict, walked out Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart.
value.literal: That day the crown prince roamed the Mystic Garden; hearing envoys arrived he changed clothes, exited Chongxian Gate, twice bowed receiving the edict, walked out Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart.

value.zh: 澹以兵仗送太子妃王氏、三皇孫于金墉城，考竟謝淑妃及太子保林蔣俊。
value.en: Dan escorted Crown Princess Wang and the three imperial grandsons to Jinyong under armed guard, and interrogated Consort Xie and the crown prince’s Lady Baolin Jiang Jun to death.
value.literal: Dan escorted Crown Princess Wang and the three imperial grandsons to Jinyong under armed guard, and interrogated Consort Xie and the crown prince’s Lady Baolin Jiang Jun to death.

value.zh: 明年正月，賈后又使黃門自首，欲與太子為逆。
value.en: Next New Year Jia staged a Yellow Gate confession implicating Yu.
value.literal: The next first month Empress Jia again had a Yellow Gate confess plotting rebellion with the crown prince.

value.zh: 詔以黃門首辭班示公卿。
value.en: An edict circulated the Yellow Gate eunuch’s confession among the dukes and ministers.
value.literal: An edict circulated the confession among dukes and ministers.

value.zh: 又遣澹以千兵防送太子，更幽于許昌宮之別坊，令治書御史劉振持節守之。
value.en: She further sent Dan with a thousand troops to escort the crown prince, moving him to a separate compound of Xuchang palace under Supervising Secretary Liu Zhen with insignia.
value.literal: She further sent Dan with a thousand troops to escort the crown prince, moving him to a separate compound of Xuchang palace under Supervising Secretary Liu Zhen with insignia.

value.zh: 先是，有童謠曰：「東宮馬子莫聾空，前至臘月纏汝閤。」
value.en: Earlier a children's rhyme ran: "Eastern Palace foals—don't plug your ears empty; come twelfth month they'll twine your chamber."
value.literal: Earlier a children's rhyme ran: 'Eastern Palace foals—don't plug your ears empty; come twelfth month they'll twine your chamber.'

value.zh: 又曰：「南風起兮吹白沙，遙望魯國郁嵯峨，千歲髑髏生齒牙。」
value.en: Another went: 'South wind rises blowing white sand; far off Lu kingdom gloomy and tall; thousand-year skulls sprout teeth.'
value.literal: Another went: 'South wind rises blowing white sand; far off Lu kingdom gloomy and tall; thousand-year skulls sprout teeth.'

value.zh: 南風，后名；
value.en: South Wind' meant Empress Jia.
value.literal: South Wind' was the empress's name.

value.zh: 沙門，太子小字也。
value.en: 'Shamen' was the crown prince's childhood byname.
value.literal: 'Shamen' was the crown prince's childhood byname.

value.zh: 太子既廢非其罪，眾情憤怨。
value.en: Injustice against Yu enraged the capital.
value.literal: After the crown prince was deposed without crime, popular feeling seethed with anger.

value.zh: 右衛督司馬雅，宗室之疏屬也，與常從督許超並有寵于太子，二人深傷之，說趙王倫謀臣孫秀曰：「國無適嗣，社稷將危，大臣之禍必起。
value.en: Right Guard Commandant Sima Ya, a distant kinsman of the imperial house, and Attendant Commandant Xu Chao, both favorites of the crown prince, grieved deeply; they told Sun Xiu, stratagemist to Lun, Prince of Zhao: "The state has no true heir—altar and grain will be imperiled; great ministers' disaster is sure to rise.
value.literal: Right Guard Commandant Sima Ya, a distant kinsman of the imperial house, and Attendant Commandant Xu Chao, both favorites of the crown prince, grieved deeply; they told Sun Xiu, stratagemist to Lun, Prince of Zhao: 'The state has no true heir—altar and grain will be imperiled; great ministers' disaster is sure to rise.

value.zh: 而公奉事中宮，與賈后親密，太子之廢，皆云豫知，一旦事起，禍必及矣。
value.en: "You serve the empress and are close to her. Everyone says you knew in advance of the prince’s deposition. If trouble breaks out, disaster will surely reach you too."
value.literal: You serve the inner palace in the empress's confidence; all say you foreknew the crown prince's deposition—should trouble erupt, disaster will reach you too.

value.zh: 何不先謀之！」
value.en: Why not plot first!"
value.literal: Why not plot first!'

value.zh: 秀言于趙王倫，倫深納焉。
value.en: Sun Xiu sold the plot to Sima Lun.
value.literal: Xiu reported to Lun, Prince of Zhao, and Lun accepted fully.

value.zh: 計既定，而秀說倫曰：「太子為人剛猛，若得志之日，必肆其情性矣。
value.en: With the plan set, Xiu said to Lun, "The crown prince is by nature rigid and fierce; if he gains his will he will certainly give free rein to his temper.
value.literal: With the plan set, Xiu said to Lun, 'The crown prince is by nature rigid and fierce; if he gains his will he will certainly give free rein to his temper.

value.zh: 明公素事賈后，街談巷議，皆以公為賈氏之黨。
value.en: Lun was branded Jia's man.
value.literal: You have long served Empress Jia; street talk names you a Jia partisan.

value.zh: 今雖欲建大功于太子，太子雖將含忍宿忿，必不能加賞於公，當謂公逼百姓之望，翻覆以免罪耳。
value.en: Yu would not thank Lun for a late defection.
value.literal: Now even if you wish to build great merit for the crown prince, though he may swallow old rage for a time he cannot reward you—he will think you only reversed under popular pressure to escape blame.

value.zh: 若有瑕釁，猶不免誅。
value.en: One slip and Lun's head would roll.
value.literal: If any flaw appears you will still not escape execution.

value.zh: 不若遷延卻期，賈后必害太子，然後廢賈后，為太子報仇，猶足以為功，乃可以得志。」
value.en: Better delay: Empress Jia is sure to harm the crown prince; then depose Jia, avenge the crown prince—merit enough to win your will."
value.literal: Better delay: Empress Jia is sure to harm the crown prince; then depose Jia, avenge the crown prince—merit enough to win your will.'

value.zh: 倫然之。
value.en: Lun assented.
value.literal: Lun agreed.

value.zh: 秀因使反間，言殿中人欲廢賈后，迎太子。
value.en: Sun Xiu spread rumors of a palace plot to restore Yu.
value.literal: Xiu therefore launched counter-espionage, saying men of the palace meant to depose Empress Jia and welcome the crown prince.

value.zh: 賈后聞之憂怖，乃使太醫令程據合巴豆杏子丸。
value.en: Jia panicked and had Cheng Ju mix purgative poison.
value.literal: When the empress heard it she was terrified and ordered Court Physician-in-Chief Cheng Ju to compound croton and apricot-kernel pills.

value.zh: 三月，矯詔使黃門孫慮齋至許昌以害太子。
value.en: Third month a fake edict sent Sun Lü to kill Yu at Xuchang.
value.literal: In the third month a forged edict sent Yellow Gate Sun Lü to Xuchang to murder the crown prince.

value.zh: 初，太子恐見鴆，恆自煮食於前。
value.en: Yu had cooked for himself to avoid cup poison.
value.literal: Earlier the crown prince had feared being poisoned and always cooked his own food before him.

value.zh: 慮以告劉振，振乃徙太子于小坊中，絕不與食，宮中猶於牆壁上過食與太子。
value.en: Lü reported this to Liu Zhen, who moved the crown prince to a small compound and denied him food. Palace personnel still passed food to him over the walls.
value.literal: Lü reported to Liu Zhen; Zhen thereupon moved the crown prince to a small ward, cut off all food, yet the palace still passed food over the wall to the crown prince.

value.zh: 慮乃逼太子以藥，太子不肯服，因如廁，慮以藥杵椎殺之，太子大呼，聲聞於外。
value.en: Sun Lü beat Yu to death in the latrine with a pestle—screams escaped.
value.literal: Lü then forced medicine on the crown prince; the crown prince refused to swallow; while using the privy Lü killed him with a medicine pestle; the crown prince cried loudly—the sound carried outside.

value.zh: 時年二十三。
value.en: He died at twenty-three.
value.literal: He was twenty-three sui.

value.zh: 將以庶人禮葬之，賈后表曰：「遹不幸喪亡，傷其迷悖，又早短折，悲痛之懷，不能自己。
value.en: They proposed burying him by commoner rites; Empress Jia memorialized: "Yu has unfortunately died—I mourn his confusion and error and early cutting-off; grief overwhelms me.
value.literal: They proposed burying him by commoner rites; Empress Jia memorialized: 'Yu has unfortunately died—I mourn his confusion and error and early cutting-off; grief overwhelms me.

value.zh: 妾私心冀其刻肌刻骨，更思孝道，規為稽顙，正其名號。
value.en: I privately hoped he would take the lesson deeply to heart and reflect anew on filial duty; a plea in prostration was intended to restore his title.
value.literal: I privately hoped he would take the lesson deeply to heart and reflect anew on filial duty; a plea in prostration was intended to restore his title.

value.zh: 此志不遂，重以酸恨。
value.en: She claimed thwarted maternal hopes.
value.literal: That aim failed—doubly bitter regret.

value.zh: 遹雖罪在莫大，猶王者子孫，便以匹庶送終，情實憐湣，特乞天恩，賜以王禮。
value.en: She asked royal burial despite his crimes.
value.literal: Though Yu's guilt was utmost he remains an imperial grandson—to dispatch him as a mere commoner truly pity—may Heaven grant kingly burial.

value.zh: 妾誠暗淺不識禮義，不勝至情，冒昧陳聞。」
value.en: Your servant is dull and shallow, ignorant of ritual propriety, overwhelmed by utmost feeling—rashly venturing to memorialize."
value.literal: Your servant is dull and shallow, ignorant of ritual propriety, overwhelmed by utmost feeling—rashly venturing to memorialize.'

value.zh: 詔以廣陵王禮葬之。
value.en: The court buried him as Guangling prince.
value.literal: An edict buried him with rites due Prince of Guangling.

value.zh: 及賈庶人死，乃誅劉振、孫慮、程據等，冊復太子曰：「皇帝使使持節、兼司空、衛尉伊策故皇太子之靈曰：嗚呼！
value.en: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: "The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!
value.literal: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: 'The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!

value.zh: 維爾少資岐嶷之質，荷先帝殊異之寵，大啟土宇，奄有淮陵。
value.en: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.
value.literal: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.

value.zh: 朕奉遵遺旨，越建爾儲副，以光顯我祖宗。
value.en: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.
value.literal: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.

value.zh: 祗爾德行，以從保傅，事親孝敬，禮無違者。
value.en: You were to revere virtuous conduct and follow your tutors, serve your parents with filial respect, and never violate ritual.
value.literal: I charged you to follow tutors in virtue, serving parents with filial respect—ritual unbreached.

value.zh: 而朕昧於凶構，致爾於非命之禍，俾申生、孝己復見於今。
value.en: Yet I failed to perceive wicked intrigues and brought you to an unnatural death, so that Shen Sheng and Xiao Ji appeared again in our time.
value.literal: Yet I, dim to vicious plots, brought you to the misfortune of untimely death, making Shen Sheng and Xiao Ji again appear in our day.

value.zh: 賴宰相賢明，人神憤怨，用啟朕心，討厥有罪，咸伏其辜。
value.en: Fortunately, wise ministers and the indignation of men and spirits opened my eyes; I punished the guilty, and all paid the penalty for their crimes.
value.literal: Thanks to wise ministers, human and spirit alike resented, opening my heart to punish the guilty—each has met sentence.

value.zh: 何補於荼毒冤魂酷痛哉？
value.en: But how can that make amends for the cruel suffering inflicted upon your wronged spirit?
value.literal: What use mending poisoned wronged souls' cruel pain?

value.zh: 是用忉怛悼恨，震動於五內。
value.en: Thus I grieve in anguish and regret, shaken to my innermost being.
value.literal: Therefore grief tears my vitals and shakes my five inner organs.

value.zh: 今追復皇太子喪禮，反葬京畿，祠乙太牢。
value.en: Now I restore the funeral rites due the crown prince, return your burial to the capital region, and offer a full tailao sacrifice of ox, sheep, and pig.
value.literal: Now I restore the funeral rites due the crown prince, return your burial to the capital region, and offer a full tailao sacrifice of ox, sheep, and pig.

value.zh: 魂而有靈，尚獲爾心。」
value.en: If soul possesses awareness may it receive this heart."
value.literal: If soul possesses awareness may it receive this heart.'

value.zh: 帝為太子服長子斬衰，群臣齊衰，使尚書和郁率東宮官屬具吉凶之制，迎太子喪于許昌。
value.en: Court mourned and fetched Yu's bier from Xu.
value.literal: The emperor wore unhemmed mourning for the crown prince as for an eldest son; the ministers wore hemmed mourning. He sent Minister He Yu to lead the Eastern Palace officials in preparing the prescribed auspicious and mourning rites and bringing the crown prince's bier back from Xuchang.

value.zh: 劉毅
value.en: Liu Yi.
value.literal: Liu Yi.

value.zh: 劉毅，字希樂，彭城沛人也。
value.en: Liu Yi, whose courtesy name was Xile, came from Pei in the Pengcheng region.
value.literal: Liu Yi, courtesy name Xile, was a native of Pei in Pengcheng commandery.

value.zh: 曾祖距，廣陵相。
value.en: His great-grandfather Liu Ju had served as chancellor of Guangling.
value.literal: His great-grandfather Ju had been Chancellor of Guangling.

value.zh: 叔父鎮，左光祿大夫。
value.en: His uncle Liu Zhen had held the post of left household grandee with the golden seal and purple ribbon.
value.literal: His uncle Zhen had been Left Household Grandee of Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

value.zh: 毅少有大志，不修家人產業，仕為州從事，桓弘以為中兵參軍屬。
value.en: From his youth Liu Yi aimed high and kept no careful household estate. He entered service as a provincial clerk, and Huan Hong made him an aide in the central army staff.
value.literal: In youth Yi cherished great ambitions, did not attend to household property, and took office as a provincial clerk; Huan Hong appointed him subordinate to the central army adjutant.

value.zh: 桓玄篡位，毅與劉裕、何無忌、魏詠之等起義兵，密謀討玄，毅討徐州刺史桓修于京口、青州刺史桓弘于廣陵。
value.en: After Huan Xuan seized the throne, Liu Yi joined Liu Yu, He Wuji, Wei Yongzhi, and others in raising a loyal army and secretly planning to bring Huan Xuan down. Liu Yi himself struck at Inspector of Xuzhou Huan Xiu at Jingkou and Inspector of Qingzhou Huan Hong at Guangling.
value.literal: When Huan Xuan usurped the throne, Yi together with Liu Yu, He Wuji, Wei Yongzhi, and others raised loyal troops, secretly plotting to punish Xuan; Yi attacked Xuzhou Inspector Huan Xiu at Jingkou and Qingzhou Inspector Huan Hong at Guangling.

value.zh: 裕率毅等至竹裏，玄使其將皇甫敷、吳甫之北距義軍，遇之于江乘，臨陣斬甫之，進至羅落橋，又斬敷首。
value.en: Liu Yu brought Liu Yi and the rest as far as Zhuli. Huan Xuan dispatched his generals Huangfu Fu and Wu Fuzhi to block the loyal forces from the north. They met at Jiangsheng, where Wu Fuzhi was beheaded in the fighting. The army pushed on to Luoluo Bridge and there took Huangfu Fu’s head as well.
value.literal: Yu led Yi and the others to Zhuli; Xuan sent his generals Huangfu Fu and Wu Fuzhi north to block the loyal army, met them at Jiangsheng, beheaded Fuzhi on the field, advanced to Luoluo Bridge, and also cut off Fu’s head.

value.zh: 玄大懼，使桓謙、何澹之屯覆舟山。
value.en: Huan Xuan panicked and ordered Huan Qian and He Danzhi to camp at Mount Fuzhou.
value.literal: Xuan was greatly frightened and had Huan Qian and He Danzhi encamp at Mount Fuzhou.

value.zh: 毅等軍至蔣山，裕使羸弱登山，多張旗幟，玄不之測，益以危懼。
value.en: When Liu Yi’s men reached Mount Jiang, Liu Yu sent feebler troops up the slopes with a forest of banners. Huan Xuan could not read their strength and only grew more alarmed.
value.literal: When Yi and the others reached Mount Jiang, Yu had the weak climb the hill and raise many banners; Xuan could not fathom it and grew still more fearful.

value.zh: 謙等士卒多北府人，素懾伏裕，莫敢出鬥。
value.en: Most of Huan Qian’s troops were Northern Headquarters veterans who had always feared Liu Yu, and none would step forward to offer battle.
value.literal: Many of Qian’s soldiers were men of the Northern Headquarters and had long stood in awe of Yu; none dared come out to fight.

value.zh: 裕與毅等分為數隊，進突謙陣，皆殊死戰，無不一當百。
value.en: Liu Yu and Liu Yi split into several columns and hurled themselves at Huan Qian’s formation. Every man fought as if his life depended on it, each worth a hundred ordinary soldiers.
value.literal: Yu together with Yi and the others divided into several columns, charged Qian’s line, and all fought to the death, each man worth a hundred.

value.zh: 時東北風急，義軍放火，煙塵張天，鼓噪之音震駭京邑，謙等諸軍一時奔散。
value.en: A stiff northeasterly wind was blowing. The loyal army kindled fires; smoke and dust blotted out the sky, and the roar of drums and war cries shook the capital. Huan Qian’s army scattered in a single rush.
value.literal: At that time a fierce wind blew from the northeast; the loyal army set fires, smoke and dust filled the sky, and the din of drums and shouts shook the capital; Qian’s host broke and fled all at once.

value.zh: 玄既西走，裕以毅為冠軍將軍、青州刺史，與何無忌、劉道規躡玄。
value.en: Once Huan Xuan had fled westward, Liu Yu named Liu Yi champion general and inspector of Qingzhou and, with He Wuji and Liu Daogui, set off in pursuit.
value.literal: After Xuan fled west, Yu appointed Yi Champion General and Inspector of Qingzhou, and together with He Wuji and Liu Daogui they pressed Xuan.

value.zh: 玄逼帝及琅邪王西上，毅與道規及下邳太守孟懷玉等追及玄，戰于崢嶸洲。
value.en: Huan Xuan drove the emperor and the prince of Langye upriver. Liu Yi, Liu Daogui, and Xiapi prefect Meng Huaiyu caught him and gave battle at Zhengrong Islet.
value.literal: Xuan forced the emperor and the Prince of Langye westward; Yi together with Daogui and Xiapi Prefect Meng Huaiyu overtook Xuan and fought at Zhengrong Islet.

value.zh: 毅乘風縱火。
value.en: Liu Yi used the wind to his advantage and set the enemy fleet ablaze.
value.literal: Yi exploited the wind to spread fire.

value.zh: 盡銳爭先，玄眾大潰，燒輜重夜走。
value.en: His picked troops vied to lead the charge. Huan Xuan’s army collapsed completely, torched its baggage, and slipped away under cover of darkness.
value.literal: With every elite vying to be first, Xuan’s host was utterly routed; they burned the baggage train and fled by night.

value.zh: 玄將郭銓、劉雅等襲陷尋陽，毅遣武威將軍劉懷肅討平之。
value.en: Huan Xuan’s generals Guo Quan and Liu Ya seized Xunyang by surprise. Liu Yi sent General Who Displays Might Liu Huaisu, who crushed them and restored order.
value.literal: Xuan’s generals Guo Quan and Liu Ya raided and took Xunyang; Yi sent General Who Displays Might Liu Huaisu and pacified them.

value.zh: 若夫穹昊垂景，少微以躔其次；
value.en: Consider how the high heavens let fall their light, and the hermit star Shaowei keeps to its station in the sky.
value.literal: As for the vaulted heaven lowering its radiance, Shaowei thereby treads its place among them;

value.zh: 《文》《系》探幽，貞遁以成其象。
value.en: The "Appended Remarks" and "Wings" sound out what lies in shadow, and the hexagram of principled retreat gives that stance its perfect emblem.
value.literal: The "Wen" and "Xi" plumb the hidden; steadfast withdrawal completes their image.
